fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. Saul, the son of Kish, was "…a head taller than any of the people." That comes right after the text calls him choice and handsome, without equal among the Israelites. I'm a cookie stamper, so a head taller than anyone is a view I'll never know.
Not quite. The servant doesn't pull out any spices. He says, "I have here in my hand a quarter shekel of silver." Silver is what he offers to give the man of God.

A gold ring would've been fancy, but the text doesn't have one. The servant offers "…a quarter shekel of silver." It's a small gift, but it answers Saul's worry about having nothing to take the man of God.
Good guess, but priest isn't the word the writer uses. The text says "…the prophet of today was formerly called the seer." Seer and prophet go together here, and priest doesn't.

You've got it. The LORD tells Samuel, "At this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin…" And Saul is a Benjamite, the son of Kish, who was from Benjamin. The LORD had told Samuel the day before Saul ever arrived.

That's the word. The LORD says, "…you are to anoint him ruler over My people Israel…" Saul came looking for donkeys, and the LORD has something else in mind. The man walking up the hill with a servant is about to get a new job.

Not quite, baker. Prophets do show up later in this passage, so I get the guess. But the LORD tells Samuel to anoint this man "…ruler over My people Israel…" That's the job on the table, and it's a big one for a man who just went out to find donkeys.

Samuel doesn't mention next week. He tells Saul he shall eat with him today, and says, "…when I send you off in the morning, I will tell you all that is in your heart." The invitation is for today's meal.

Saul did worry about his father earlier, but that's not his answer here. He says, "Am I not a Benjamite from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of Benjamin?" He calls his clan the least of all the clans of Benjamin.

You've got it. Samuel "…seated them in the place of honor among those who were invited—about thirty in all." That puts a man who came looking for donkeys in the place of honor. The servant is seated there too.

Not quite. Nobody is told to wait in the corner. The text says Samuel seated them "…in the place of honor…" Saul and his servant came in as guests, seated among those who were invited, about thirty in all.

Not quite, baker. Samuel says the portion "…was set apart for you." and "…has been kept for you for this occasion…" He says it was kept for Saul from the time he invited the people. It was put aside before Saul ever sat down.
Not quite. Samuel says he'll reveal "…the word of God." That's the reason Saul stays behind, not a blessing for the trip. Samuel has the servant go on ahead, so the two of them are left alone.

That's right, baker. Samuel "…took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him…" That's what anointing looks like here. Then he asks, "Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?"
Not quite, baker. The text says Samuel "…poured it on Saul’s head…" The oil goes on Saul, and that's how he's anointed. Then Samuel asks, "Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?"
Samuel doesn't hand over the flask. He "…poured it on Saul’s head…" It's an anointing, not a gift to carry home. Then he asks, "Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?"

You've got it. Samuel says the three men "…will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands." The three are carrying goats, bread and wine, and the loaves are what Samuel says they'll give him.
The men are carrying young goats, so I see the mix-up. But Samuel says they'll give Saul "…two loaves of bread…" The goats aren't part of what he says they'll give.

That's it. Samuel says, "Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them…" He says the prophets will be preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres. Saul joins in with something much bigger than an instrument.

Harps are in the picture, but Samuel never says Saul gets handed one. He says, "…the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them…" The harps come before the prophets, and nothing in the text hands one to Saul.

Not quite. Samuel says, "…you will be transformed into a different person." That's part of what he tells Saul about Gibeah. It comes right after he says the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon Saul and he will prophesy.
Kish is Saul's father, and Samuel does say the men will tell Saul that Kish has started worrying about him. But Samuel says, "…for God is with you." That's the one who's with Saul.

That's right. Samuel says, "…surely I will come to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings." He also says, "Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do." So Saul is told to wait for instructions.
Not quite, baker. The text says nothing about Saul's face. It says, "…God changed Saul’s heart…" and that happens as he turns to leave Samuel.
Not quite. The text says, "…all the signs came to pass that day." That's one day, not weeks. Samuel's list was long, and it all fit into that one day.

Not quite, baker. The people who had known Saul ask, "What has happened to the son of Kish?" Nothing in that question is about his return. I think they're surprised by what they see, since they'd just watched him prophesying with the prophets.
